notes.title: Sands of Time DLC – Development Update
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]It has been a busy stretch of production, and we want to take a moment to share where things stand with the [i]Sands of Time[/i] DLC for [b]Elleria: Book I[/b].[/p][p]The DLC has grown into something much larger than originally envisioned—expanding the world of Elleria with new lore, cinematic moments, and original music. A great deal of work is going into ensuring the [b]fantasy atmosphere remains deep, immersive, and true to the tone of the main game.[/b][/p][p]Here’s what’s been happening:[/p][list][*][p][b]Visuals & Cinematics:[/b] We’ve been creating new renders, animations, especially environmental ones and vision sequences that will bring the desert setting and its mysteries to life.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Music & Atmosphere:[/b] A fully new soundtrack is in progress, tailored to match both the awe-inspiring and ominous tones of the story. As always, being very firm about music and believing it contributes heavily to overall atmosphere and story, Sands of Time currently stands above 20 soundtracks tailored for it.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Narrative & Lore:[/b] The [i]Sands of Time[/i] storyline expands on themes of fate, time, and forgotten powers tying directly into Eliot’s journey and what awaits beyond Book I.[/p][/*][/list][p]This DLC is not just an “add-on”—it’s part of a larger vision leading toward [b]Book II[/b], giving both long-time players and newcomers more reasons to dive deeper into Elleria’s universe. Rest assured we're currently working [b]way[/b] over the clock, to deliver this as fast as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]And now for something special we’re sharing one of the [i]Sands of Time[/i] OST tracks:[/p][p]🎶 [b]Vaerith – The Veiled Daughter[/b][/p][p]This piece captures her presence perfectly: majestic, inevitable, and quietly awe-inspiring. It’s one of our personal favorites, and we can’t wait for you to hear it![/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="CTxoohjuDS8;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Clearing Misunderstandings
notes.notes:
[p]Usually, I wouldn’t waste time on this, but I think it’s worth addressing. I’ve seen recent reviews and outside comments about Elleria that misinterpret our words, twist them into “facts,” and spread them around as if they’re the truth. Let’s clear this up.[/p][p]One recent review said:[/p][quote][p]“Tried to load my game and it crashed. I commend the developer for their honesty in their recent post but saying not enough people bought my game so I just finished it quickly is not great marketing and I won't be buying anymore of these.”[/p][/quote][p]Here’s the reality: Elleria was not “finished quickly” or abandoned due to sales. The Wheel of Fate DLC was delivered as planned, with multiple patches, bug fixes, optimizations, and additional content after release. That’s [i]not[/i] the behavior of someone rushing a product — that’s the behavior of a developer supporting it.[/p][p]We’ve been transparent about the fact that Elleria didn’t meet the sales needed for large-scale production. That honesty is not the same thing as “I gave up.” It means I delivered the content as promised, improved it with feedback, and adjusted scope responsibly instead of promising things that couldn’t be delivered.[/p][p]And then, I see another take being spread (ironically, from piracy forums of all places):[/p][quote][p]“Elleria is being rushed just to have some kind of ‘ending’… projects can start with passion but when money is the final goal something goes wrong in the long run.”[/p][/quote][p]Let me be blunt: this is detached from [b]reality[/b]. Passion may start a project, but without funding, it [i]dies[/i]. Period. Electricity bills for rendering, software licenses, hardware upgrades, and production costs don’t vanish just because someone thinks money shouldn’t matter. That isn’t how life works.[/p][p]I’ve spent this time financing Elleria out of [u][b]my own pocket[/b][/u], [u][b]giving content away for free[/b][/u], and carrying this project far beyond what was financially reasonable. Money isn’t the “final goal” — it’s the [i]fuel[/i] that keeps the fire burning. Without it, there is no Elleria, no DLC, no continuation.[/p][p]So let’s set the record straight:[/p][list][*][p][b]Elleria was not abandoned.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Wheel of Fate was completed and patched extensively.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Sands of Time DLC is next, and Book 2 will follow.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]If acknowledging reality makes me the bad guy in some people’s eyes, so be it. I’d rather be honest than sell fairytales.[/p][p]The story continues. [b]Sands of Time is coming. Book 2 is coming. Elleria is not done.


P.S.[/b]
The moral of the story is simple: [i]passion creates, but money sustains.[/i] Without resources, there is no project, no updates, no DLCs — just silence. Electricity isn’t free, bread isn’t free, and neither is the work that goes into making a game.[/p][p]So the next time someone tries to say [b]“money shouldn’t matter”[/b] while playing hundreds of hours of work for the price of a [u]sandwich[/u] — remember that it only exists because someone paid the very real costs to make it.

The people shouting loudest that “money shouldn’t matter” are usually the ones who didn’t pay in the first place. ːsteamboredː[/p][p][/p][p]– Arcane Ink Productions[/p]

notes.title: Wheel of Fate - It's a wrap
notes.notes: [p][b]Hey everyone,[/b][/p][p][/p][p]It’s been a while—longer than I planned, and for that, I apologize. Life has a strange way of throwing up walls just when you think you're past the hardest part. The wrap-up for [i]Elleria: Wheel of Fate[/i] took more time than I wanted it to, but it’s finally here.[/p][p][/p][p]Originally, I had bigger plans for this DLC. There were scenes, sequences, even a few side branches I wanted to include… but the window I had set aside for production simply ran out. Some things had to be cut, reworked, or left behind. That said, I still think [i]Wheel of Fate[/i] turned out to be a solid expansion to Elleria’s lore. We introduced new characters, deepened the world, and gave players some weighty choices that will carry over into what comes next.[/p][p][/p][p]On a more honest note—[i]Elleria[/i] has more or less hit its ceiling in terms of sales. It hasn’t done terribly, but it hasn’t justified further large-scale production in the way I’d hoped. And while not everything should be about money, the unfortunate truth is: it’s a necessary evil when it comes to keeping a project alive.[/p][p]At one point, I was genuinely considering scrapping everything moving forward and letting the story end here.[/p][p][/p][p]But I changed my mind.[/p][p][/p][p]Where this started with [i]I[/i], there is now [i]we[/i]. We’re trying to push through the chaos, we’re still here—and we’re still on top of it. [i]Elleria[/i] will continue.[/p][p][/p][p]That said, [i]Sands of Time[/i] (the next DLC) will be more fast-paced, more condensed, and yes—some content will need to be trimmed. The same will apply to [i]Book 2[/i]. Due to the financial flop of the game overall, we’ll be cutting back on certain aspects—but we’ll still do our best to make it worth your time.[/p][p][/p][p]I won’t pretend [i]Elleria[/i] is perfect—it’s rough around the edges in places, and I’m very aware of that. But I’m still proud of it. Writing this story has been a wild ride, and honestly? A fun one. I don’t have a firm date for [i]Book 2[/i] yet, but [i]Sands of Time[/i] should be arriving—hopefully—before Christmas.[/p][p]After that, we’ll be shifting focus back to [i]Valenza Family[/i]. If you want to know more about that project, check out our website:[/p][p][/p][p]🌐 [url="https://arcaneinkproductions.com"]https://arcaneinkproductions.com[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Or visit the Steam page directly: 🔗 [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3519940?utm_source=chatgpt.com"]Valenza Family on Steam[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Thank you to everyone who’s been here for the journey. Whether you discovered [i]Elleria[/i] at launch or just recently, it means a lot that you’ve stuck with us through it all.[/p][p][/p][p]See you soon in [i]Sands of Time[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][b]– Arcane Ink Productions[/b][/p]

notes.title: Patchageddon: Renderer Wars & More! v1.3.3
notes.notes:
[h1]Renderer Selector & The Blight Cleansing Patch[/h1]

Gather around Paladins!

Today’s patching spree is all about stability, bug-smashing, and putting an end to the renderer corruption The Blight has been spreading across your systems! 

🧙 [b]New: Graphics Mode Selector[/b]

On first launch (or after resetting Preferences), the game now asks which arcane rendering method you'd like to trust.

[b]Your choices:[/b]

[list]
[*] Auto – Let the Sanctum divine the best choice.
[*] ANGLE – Blessed path for modern GPUs.
[*] OpenGL 2 (GL2) – For older relics that still endure.
[*] OpenGL (GL) – Ancient fallback—only if all else fails.
[/list]

If you've encountered black screens, crashes, or strange artifacting, this selector might be your salvation.

📜 [b]Textbox Opacity Purification[/b]
Some players reported crashes when adjusting textbox opacity.
Turns out The Blight had its claws in the UI.
We’ve exorcised the issue. The setting now initializes properly and no longer causes chaos.

🛠️ [b]General Cleansing & Safety Rites[/b]

[b]Removed lingering renderer code corrupted by the Old Code.[/b]

Ensured that all renderer choices are preserved safely. No more overwriting your sacred save files.

✅ [b]This patch should:[/b]

[list]
[*] Eliminate crashes caused by incompatible or cursed graphics renderers.
[*] Resolve opacity-related exceptions haunting the Preferences screen.
[*] Make startup smoother for all chosen warriors of Elleria.
[/list]


🧹 [b]IMPORTANT[/b]:
[u]If you played a previous version, delete your persistent data and reinstall the game to fully purge any lingering corruption.[/u]

[i]The Blight remembers. But now, so do we.[/i]


[i]"The Blight spreads no more… for now."[/i]

notes.title: v1.3.2 [HOTFIX] – The Renderer Rebellion
notes.notes:
[h1]v1.3.2 – Wheel of Fate [Hotfix][/h1]

Some players encountered a rare but critical crash after naming their character, caused by:

[u]TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'[/u]

[b]Why did it happen?[/b]

[i]This occurs only on specific setups where a combination of GPU drivers + Ren'Py’s default (gl3/ANGLE) renderer + certain UI transforms causes instability — particularly on Steam Deck and newer GPUs.[/i]

[b]Fixes in this hotfix:
[/b]
[list]
[*] 🔧 Renderer fallback updated to use gl2 and a stable 60 FPS cap. 
[/list]

This improves compatibility for Steam Deck, Linux, and modern graphics cards. 
No performance impact for players who weren’t affected.

If you’re still experiencing issues, you can also manually launch the game with this in your Steam launch options: 

--renderer gl2 --framerate 60

notes.title: Elleria - Wheel of Fate DLC Gameplay Preview

After completing Book 1 of Elleria, I couldn’t shake the feeling that there were aspects I left unfinished, elements that might have left a bad taste. That’s why the Wheel of Fate DLC exists, and War Table idea has been scrapped—to offer a chance to redeem those choices, to enhance the story and lore, and to give you a deeper, more impactful journey. This DLC isn’t just about strategy—it’s about shaping the future with every decision, righting some of the wrongs that lingered from the first book.

It will be bigger, better, and hopefully you'll give it a shot!

notes.title: Book 1 End - Mind the giant post!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101741/c3568f3dccc00077511494ed3bb0dd3cefdfdecc.png[/img]

Whew... it’s been a long journey for me, personally. I’ve got about five hundred things to say—probably more, knowing myself—but I’m not sure where to start or where to finish. So, let’s see how this goes.

First and most importantly: it’s here, it’s done. The final chapter of Elleria and Book 1 is complete and out of the way. I’ll admit, I feel like I could’ve pushed a bit more or added a few extra touches here and there, but, well... what we want and what life throws at us don’t always line up. Recent health issues have hit me like a punch in the face. But hey, it’s not all doom and gloom.

I mentioned this in my last post, but I’ll say it again. For you, this means a giant chunk of the story is done and dusted. For me, though, it just means a lot more work ahead. While I’m happy and satisfied to have accomplished so much in such a short time, it doesn’t mean, “Oh, here you go, moving on.” Unfortunately, I can’t leave certain things in their current state, which means even more work on my plate.

Let’s talk about The False War DLC—yes, that one. By all means, and just to confirm, it will be free. You’ll get it with the Elleria update you already own. It’s not a massive addition, but it’s still a story worth telling, exploring events from the past and diving into Eliot’s background.

But that’s not all. I’ve got a long to-do list and plenty of polishing to take care of. 

I wish I could say I’m completely happy with Elleria and how it turned out, but I’d be lying. The truth is... I’m not. But I’ll work on it. There are parts I loved more than others, and parts I hated more than others. It’s been one giant learning experience for me. And, as they say, you can’t buy experience—which is exactly why it’s so valuable!

From this point onward, you can expect bits and pieces to come and go as I work toward a level of personal satisfaction with this massive chunk of Book 1. I could dive into all the details, but honestly, I’d probably end up writing you another book instead of a single post about my plans. That said, if you’re part of the Discord, you’re likely already in the loop on what I’m planning and everything else tied to it.

That being said, I’m always here and available for any questions, answers, or any kind of inquiries, really. So don’t hesitate to speak up—I don’t bite. (Well, sometimes.) Got suggestions, ideas, wishes, or wants? Just toss them my way. While I can’t promise I’ll implement everything, that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t share. Feedback is a developer’s bread and butter—without it, we’ve got nothing.

I’ve got so much more I want to say, but honestly, for most of you, this post is probably already too long, and you’re ready to punch me for writing it. I don’t blame you—I get it! Nobody likes a wall of text. But hey, sometimes it’s necessary.

Once again, I know this sounds like a repeat of my last post. I know. I know. I’m fully aware of the mistakes, the things that could’ve been done better, and the things that can be done better. I’ll do my best to improve what’s within my ability. This whole process has been a massive learning experience for me—something I’ll carry with me into Book 2 of Elleria to make it far better than what Book 1 is.

Elleria Book 1 is rough. It has its moments, and it has its downsides. But on a personal level—speaking only for myself—I’m satisfied with it.

When I started this, I didn’t have any specific intent. For me, it was my story—a reflection of my thoughts on our world, my opinions, and my views. I turned it into something meaningful for myself, and then I decided to share it with the world because… well, why not?

So, despite its flaws—flaws that can be improved on—I’m happy with it.

It’s not everyone’s cup of tea, and I respect that. But the important thing is... it doesn’t have to be. It’s mine. And I’ll gladly share this cup with those who want a sip, while respecting those who don’t. Whatever the case may be, I hope you enjoy the conclusion of Book 1 and Chapter 5.

It’s been a long road, and honestly, my car tires are flat, and I’m out of fuel. But don’t worry—I’ve got a mechanic. I’ll see you around sooner than you might think.

Once again, don’t hesitate to reach out to me on Discord. I’m always there and available for chit-chat, questions, or anything in between!

notes.title: Chapter 4, News and what's next!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101741/af1b20efa639f64790f85f77a474ff629b1d5c30.png[/img]

Hello there! It’s been a year without updates (I know, what a cliché joke, but I couldn’t help it).

Finally, Chapter 4 is here! I wish I could’ve finished it earlier—I really intended to—but I was hit by some misfortunes and health issues that badly steered my ship off course.

I’m still not at one hundred percent, but with the help of some medication, I was able to find the strength to sit down and resume my work. For now, let’s hope things stay that way on the health front.

Moving on to Elleria itself, it’s important to note that Chapter 5 will be the last and final update for Elleria Book 1—that’s going to be a wrap from me. However, that doesn’t mean your journey is over, and it certainly doesn’t mean my work is done.

Even without feedback from you kind folks, I’m well aware of many issues that need to be addressed, and my to-do list is anything but short.

Once Chapter 5 is finished (which is my main focus at the moment), I’ll deliver another update before Elleria leaves Early Access and proceeds to full release.

I also plan to go back and rewrite or rework Chapters I and II so they’re on par with Chapters III and onward. Frankly, the writing can’t even compare right now—Chapters I and II make the rest of the game look bad by comparison.

There are also a few more items on my to-do list. While I’ll say upfront that Elleria – Book II won’t be started right away, rest assured there’s something else in the works!

With Elleria Book 1 wrapped, I’ll be focusing on adding more content to the game. I’d like to share a bit of information about what that will involve.

One of the upcoming updates will focus on the war table system—a standalone update that lets you influence the game world and its political state. This will be a choice-based feature presented mostly in a textual format. It’s aimed at those who enjoy interactive, narrative-driven elements; if that’s not your cup of tea, you’re free to skip it!

With Chapter 4 comes the introduction of a new character named Silas Varros. I won’t say much more to avoid spoilers, but you’ll notice a certain aspect I’ve added that I intend to explore further.

Although this is already explained in the game, I’ll repeat it here for clarity. If you like what you see of Silas in Chapter 4, you’ll have the chance to play as him in Elleria’s DLC.

In the DLC, you’ll step into the role of a professional assassin under Eliot’s mentorship, indulging in some classic “stabby” gameplay across Elleria through multiple choice-based missions.

I could go on, but this post is already long enough! So, without further ado, I hope you enjoy Chapter 4.

As I mentioned before, I’m fully aware of Elleria’s flaws and shortcomings. Rest assured, they have not escaped the watchful gaze of Azhaq’tel, and they will be dealt with—mercilessly!

notes.title: Elleria - Upcoming & What to Expect
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101741/e5e6696234f231357560f7b25105574f8edfd9de.png[/img]

Hello lads and lasses!

With Elleria's upcoming Early Access release on November 1st, I've decided to create this brief introduction and share a few notes on what you can expect from the game in its current state.

First and foremost, Elleria is a story-heavy, story-focused game, crafted for those who love a world brimming with magic—a wholly different existence. It’s for minds that can wander in wonder, ever-expanding, ever-longing. If you're looking for the somewhat typical very hot and steamy games, I must disappoint you—this isn't one of them! [i]( Well, not in the standard sense one may be used when it comes to these! )[/i]

However, if you’re here for hours of immersive fantasy reading filled with magic, dragons, wars, and romance, drama, plot-twists and more! Then welcome! [b]Be warned, though, that Elleria's story is complex. You’ll encounter puzzles and fragments, mystery and darkness, and it’s my intent, as a writer, to encourage players to draw their own conclusions, make assumptions, think, and stay in the dark.[/b] [u]Don’t be discouraged! Remember, when it feels like nothing makes sense, that you are lost. Don't lose hope. Piece by piece things come together and you may yet find  the light you seek—the pieces of the puzzle will click into place.[/u]

[i](And if you're curious or feeling impatient, never fear! Join us on Discord. I love nothing more than debating lore and listening to theories about how the story forms and unfolds!)[/i]

While Elleria is an adult visual novel, its adult content is intended to be meaningful and immersive. That said, these scenes were not my primary focus during the extremely exhausting development process. Though they were crafted with care, they may reflect my relative inexperience with the creation tools used.

The journey hasn’t been quick or easy—ranging from hardware incompatibility to time limitations and more. Game development is a challenging road! BUT—I'm pleased to say it's improving with each update as I become more familiar with the software. The quality continues to get better, but don't expect the elaborate animations you might find in similar games just yet. Keyword: yet!

Elleria’s beginning is a bit rough around the edges. Playing through it myself, I was struck by the difference between Chapter III and earlier chapters, both in terms of visuals and writing.

I'm writing this long post because I want players to know what to expect rather than diving in blindly. I hope this helps set expectations, offers a bit of understanding for the current roughness, and gives you something to look forward to.

Elleria is a big project, and it will take time to flourish. This is why we have Early Access—to gather feedback, feedback, feedback. I can't stress enough how valuable it is to developers!

Finally, I should get back to writing, but I hope what’s available at release sparks your interest and leaves you wanting more.

See you soon!
